name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+16 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Republican territory
Incumbent Marlin Stutzman is renominated and holds a roughly three-to-one fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Stutzman at about 95% to win
No public general-election polling exists, so fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The district's R+16 lean, Stutzman's incumbency, and his clear fundraising advantage all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at roughly 95% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting any drag, there is no evidence warranting a move from the fundamentals-based margin of about 16 points Republican.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Stutzman combined with a strong Democratic fundraising quarter would be the first sign the race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 3rd District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of R+16, and incumbent Marlin Stutzman is running for reelection after easily securing renomination. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the seat as competitive, so the race is judged on underlying fundamentals.

Those fundamentals clearly favor the incumbent. Stutzman has raised roughly $959,000 to Democrat Kelly Thompson's $309,000, and outside groups have spent modestly on his behalf. Thompson retains about $104,000 on hand, giving her limited resources for a district this unfavorable. Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 95%, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin of about 16 points. Barring an unexpected external shock, Stutzman is heavily favored to hold the seat.
